target_customer: Accounting firms in the Nordics that want to serve more clients per accountant
problem: Accountants spend time on research, supplier invoice processing, reconciliations and monthly closings. Bluebook builds AI agents that automate this so a professional can serve about 200 clients instead of 20, per its YC page.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to accounting firms

founders.name: Filip Stal
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists only him and gives no employer or education. Press names additional co-founders but those names were not confirmed on the YC page, so they are not listed.

competitors.name: Semine
competitors.what: AI based accounts payable automation for finance teams
competitors.traction_then: Entered Finland in February 2024 extending an existing Norwegian business

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents for tax, VAT and accounting research plus reconciliation need accurate retrieval and integrations with Nordic accounting systems, which is standard LLM engineering with domain hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow integration inside firms creates some lock in, but general AI tools and local accounting vendors can build similar agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Aspia announced an AI initiative in May 2025 and other Nordic players launched AI accounting offers; no acquisition of Bluebook was found.

market_need_then: Nordic accounting firms face staff shortages and repetitive work. EQT Ventures reports 20+ pilots and work with 8 of the top 10 accounting firms in Sweden within months of founding.

branding.domain_note: Uses getbluebook.com; the website returned HTTP 404 when fetched in this research session, so its content was not read

brand_strength.rationale: The name evokes accounting ledgers but collides with Kelley Blue Book and Blue Book Services in search; no brand press beyond funding coverage.

outcome_analysis: Bluebook is active. It raised about $3M pre-seed in February 2025 led by EQT Ventures and reported 30 Nordic firms as users on its YC page. Early pilots with large Swedish firms suggest real pull and the AI timing helps. No later round was found, and the risk is that local incumbents and new entrants build similar agents.
notes: Amount reported as $3M total and as 2.8M euro total including 2.4M euro pre-seed by different outlets; $3M recorded as reported by tech.eu and CPA Practice Advisor. One aggregator labels the round seed. Press names Jonathan Andersson and Philip Andersson as co-founders and one source calls Philip Andersson CEO; the YC page lists only Filip Stal, so they are not recorded as founders.
